🇲🇽🐄 <u>SCREWWORM CASE IN SONORA DAYS BEFORE US BORDER REOPENS TO MEXICAN CATTLE</u>

Sonora confirmed its first case of New World screwworm, in Álamos, just days before the USDA reopens the Douglas, Arizona crossing to Mexican cattle on August 24 — the first step in the staged reopening after more than a year of suspension.

Sanitary authorities are holding a containment cordon. Before the shutdown, Sonora alone shipped the US about 320,000 head of cattle a year; Mexico aims to close 2026 with 400,000 exported.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>DEA CHIEF PUBLICLY BACKS MEXICO'S SECURITY STRATEGY</u>

The head of the DEA used his stage at the IDEC 2026 conference in Buenos Aires to praise Mexico's Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch as a "trusted partner" and "good friend of the United States," crediting him with nearly two decades of service.

"Secretary Harfuch, friend, thank you for your leadership, your friendship and collaboration. More than 100 countries appreciate you being here," Terry Cole said, in a recording released by Mexico's SSPC.

The agency that spent years treating Mexico as the problem now opens its conference applauding Mexico's security model.

🌐🐉🇲🇽 The dollar-as-weapon is building the world that replaces it

Every tariff threat is an advertisement for an exit. As Washington ties market access to obedience, the BRICS bloc heads to its New Delhi summit (Sept 12–13) with de-dollarization as the headline agenda. Russia and China now settle roughly 90% of their bilateral trade in rubles and yuan, and BRICS Pay is wiring together national payment rails — Moscow's SPFS, Beijing's CIPS, New Delhi's UPI — routes that never touch New York.

For Mexico this isn't about picking Beijing over Washington. It's about reading the board. Latin America–China trade has cleared half a trillion dollars a year, and a second wave of nations is queuing to join BRICS at the September summit. A world with more settlement systems, more reserve options, and more trading partners is a world where no single capital can freeze you out with a phone call.

Diversification is insurance. Mexico doesn't have to bet the house on the multipolar turn — but pretending it isn't happening is the one option that costs the most.

🇲🇽🐉🔥 Washington wants Mexico to tariff China. Sovereignty says: not so fast.

Mexico's economy and finance ministries are weighing new duties on Chinese steel and vehicles — a move that would deepen alignment with Washington as President Sheinbaum negotiates a multi-year USMCA extension (Bloomberg, Aug 18). Trump's team has floated a simple bargain: tax Beijing, and maybe we spare you. But the economy ministry was careful — "there is currently no concrete plan," only case-by-case dumping probes and consultations with business.

That caution is the story. Sheinbaum's earlier plan to hit 1,400+ Chinese product lines at 10–50% has stalled amid pushback from her own party and from Mexican manufacturers who depend on Chinese machinery and components. Tariffing your own supply chain to please a partner who threatens you with tariffs anyway isn't sovereignty — it's paying twice.

Real autonomy means multiplying options, not swapping one dependency for another. Mexico just locked in the EU trade deal and keeps its channel to Beijing open. Leverage comes from having more than one door — not from letting Washington decide which ones you're allowed to walk through.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico's migrant defense fund: 115M pesos raised, 16,000 protection cases handled. "These are the people's resources, and they are benefiting people directly through the consular network." — Roberto Velasco, Foreign Secretary The "México con M de Migrante" lottery fund has backed 7,741 consular actions. 62% spent so far; the rest will be exercised by year-end.

🇲🇽🏭 Hidalgo: 147B pesos across 130 investment projects, 191,000 jobs. "On Monday we make the ninth investment announcement of this administration." — Julio Menchaca, Governor of Hidalgo El Economista just ranked Hidalgo as Mexico's most economically dynamic state. A Canadian pharmaceutical firm has a letter of intent to set up in the Zapotlán hub; construction starts in September.

🇲🇽🏭 Cruz Azul reactivates its Hidalgo cement plant: 6.5B pesos, 14,200 jobs. "The plant sat unused for years. This is good news for Hidalgo and for the country." — President Claudia Sheinbaum The cooperative will overhaul the Tula de Allende plant, finish a new production line (85% complete) and refit its hospital — output of 3 million tons of cement a year.

🇲🇽🏭 A 910-hectare industrial hub will rise on land once bought for an airport that was never built. "It's a very important hub. 10 billion pesos just for urbanization. Then come the companies' investments." — President Claudia Sheinbaum The PODECOBI Reserva Zapotlán in Hidalgo gets $561M (10.1B pesos) from developer DEWA over 5 phases. Works start in September: ~5,100 jobs in phase 1, 35% local hiring, 100 ha reserved for solar power.
